samples.summary: Author-only edit/delete gate is bypassable via the direct Yorkie CRDT path, which is the primary writer
samples.evidence: `assertCommentAuthor` (comments.controller.ts:519) refuses an edit/delete the caller did not author, and `docs/design/sheets/comments.md` is amended to say the rule is now enforced server-side ("a workspace-scoped API key cannot delete somebody else's comment"). But comments live only in the CRDT and the editor writes them directly: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1322` calls `applyDeleteComment(root.sheets[this.tabId], threadId, commentId)` inside `doc.update` with no authorship check at all (same for `editComment` at :1316). Yorkie write authority is granted by `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:202` (`assertMember` → any workspace member gets `rw`) and :217 (an anonymous `editor`-role share-link visitor gets `rw`). Attack: as any workspace member — or as an anonymous holder of an editor share link — attach to `sheet-<docId>` with the ordinary client and delete or rewrite any other user's comment; the new gate never runs. The added HTTP check therefore narrows nothing an attacker cares about while making the surface read as covered. Largely a pre-existing property of the CRDT model, but this change is what turns it into a documented authorization control.

samples.summary: `parseImages` stores an arbitrary caller-supplied `src` URL with no scheme or origin validation
samples.evidence: `src: requireString(i.src, 'src')` accepts any non-empty string and `PUT .../tabs/:tabId/images` writes it verbatim into the CRDT. Every viewer of that worksheet then renders it: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-object-layer.tsx:216` sets `` and :196 `getOrLoadImage(image.src)` issues the fetch. A `write`-scoped API key can therefore plant `https://attacker.example/beacon.png` (per-viewer IP/User-Agent/referrer disclosure to a third party, and a rendering oracle for who opened the sheet) or a `data:` payload. `isTrustedWorkspaceImageUrl` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-image-url.ts:27) only prevents the share *token* being appended to a foreign URL — it does not stop the fetch. The backend's own `parseImageRef` (document-image-refs.spec.ts:26) documents that a foreign-origin `src` out of the CRDT is untrusted; the new writer is the one place that could refuse it at the door and does not. Any future server-side consumer of `SheetImage.src` (export/thumbnail) turns this into an SSRF sink.

samples.summary: Image collection is keyed by an unconstrained caller-supplied `id` and has no size cap
samples.evidence: `ws.images = {}; for (const image of images) ws.images[image.id] = image;` uses the caller's `id` string directly as an object key, and `parseImages` only requires it be non-empty and unique. `id: "__proto__"` makes the assignment mutate the container's prototype rather than create an own key (silently dropping the image and leaving a corrupted node in the CRDT); `"constructor"`/`"toString"` shadow the keys the reader's `Object.values` walk and `unwrapJson`'s `toJSON` probe rely on. `parseImages` also applies no cap on the array length, so a single 25 MB body can create an unbounded number of CRDT map entries on a document that every collaborator then loads. Hardening: reject reserved keys and bound the collection.

samples.summary: Direct `NotificationService.createFromComment` call bypasses `CommentNotificationDto` validation and the notification endpoint's throttle
samples.evidence: `this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan)` is invoked with `planCommentNotifications(...) as CommentNotificationDto[]` — a cast, so none of the class-validator constraints on `CommentNotificationDto` run (`@MaxLength(200)` on `threadId`/`commentId`, `@ArrayMaxSize(50)`, `@MaxLength(2000)` on `preview`). `threadId` on the reply/resolve/edit routes is a raw route param and `thread.id` can be any string a peer wrote into the CRDT, so an oversized value reaches `Notification.threadId` and, for `thread_resolved`, `dedupeKey = ${threadId}:resolved` — a value long enough to exceed Postgres' btree index entry limit makes the insert fail (swallowed by the catch at :207, so it degrades to lost notifications rather than a crash). The design doc hunk also records that `UserThrottlerGuard`, which gates `POST /notifications/comment`, does not apply here; only the global IP-based `ThrottlerGuard` (app.module.ts:128) remains. Validating the plan before handing it to the service would restore both.

samples.summary: Three new controllers re-implement the shared workspace-scope + type guard instead of calling `sheet-document.util.ts`
samples.evidence: `ApiV1WorksheetImagesController.assertSheetDocument` (worksheet-images.controller.ts:40) is a byte-for-byte re-statement of the exported `assertSheetDocument` in `packages/backend/src/api/v1/sheet-document.util.ts:36`, which `ApiV1TabsController` (tabs.controller.ts:51) calls in the same directory. `ApiV1SlidesController.assertSlidesDocument` (slides.controller.ts:62) and `ApiV1CommentsController.loadCommentableType` (comments.controller.ts:124) are the same lookup with a different type predicate. That util's own docblock records the cost of exactly this: "Nine controllers carried a private copy of this method ... the copies are what let the cells one go missing until #1019." All three copies are currently correct — each does pass `workspaceId` to `getDocumentOrThrow`, so there is no bypass today — but the security-relevant half of the guard (the workspace scoping that prevents cross-workspace document access) is now stated in four places instead of one.

samples.summary: Deleting the opening comment destroys other users' replies, authorized only against the opener
samples.evidence: `deleteComment` authorizes with `assertCommentAuthor(map, threadId, commentId, author)` (:502) and then `applyDeleteComment` returns `thread_deleted` when `commentId` is the opening comment, removing the whole thread. So a caller who authored only the first comment can destroy every later reply by other workspace members, having been authorized against a comment they own. This matches the editor's documented behaviour and `docs/design/sheets/comments.md`, so it is intended — noting it only because the response field `deleted: 'thread'` is the sole signal that a single-comment delete removed other people's content.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repository. `assertCommentAuthor` (comments.controller.ts:519-534) does enforce author-only edit/delete on the HTTP path, and docs/design/sheets/comments.md:32-38 was written to present this as server-side enforcement ("so a workspace-scoped API key cannot delete somebody else's comment"). But comments live only in the CRDT and the editor writes them directly with no authorship check: yorkie-store.ts:1320-1324 (deleteComment) and :1313-1318 (editComment) call applyDeleteComment/applyEditComment inside doc.update on any threadId/commentId the caller names; comments.md:242 even documents the primitive as "Caller is responsible for author check." Write authority on that path is document-level only: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:201-206 grants access to anyone passing workspaceService.assertMember (workspace.service.ts:236-243 — mere row existence, no role), and :217 grants write to an anonymous share-link visitor whose role is 'editor'. checkAttribute (:170-186) authorizes at document-key + verb granularity, so nothing inspects the comment mutation itself. Attack chain is complete: any workspace member, or an anonymous holder of an editor share link, attaches to the sheet document with an ordinary Yorkie client and edits or deletes any other user's comment; assertCommentAuthor never runs. No refutation ground applies — the code is present as described, no guard elsewhere makes it unreachable, and a bypassable authorization gate is squarely in the Security lens (authorization/access control, weakest entry point). The 'largely pre-existing' caveat does not matter under the rubric, which directs judging only whether the defect is real and blocking.
